mission: Frank v0.1 voll lauffähig auf Andreas PC

repo_freshness.collision_policy: No production parser/canonicalizer mutation from this run; unique-path evidence write only.

hypothesis: A semantically inert grammar-comment perturbation must preserve semantic AST identity while changing grammar/parser-contract identity.
counterhypothesis: Grammar bytes are intentionally part of the only canonical syntax identity; a distinct grammar-independent semantic identity is unnecessary.

experiment.name: GRAMMAR_COMMENT_IDENTITY_LAYER_PERTURBATION
experiment.method: Apply the exact hash formulas extracted from current tools/claycode_base_frontend.py and tools/claycode_base_canonicalizer.py to one fixed canonical AST while perturbing grammar bytes only by an ignored // comment. No parser execution is claimed.
experiment.interpretation: The current extracted formulas encode two identity layers in the production frontend (semantic AST versus grammar-bound contract), while the standalone canonicalizer labels its grammar-bound identity semantic_hash. This is a real identity/contract-layer divergence, not proof of wrong runtime semantics.
limitations: No Lark parse executed in this experiment.
Debian shadow is not Ubuntu target evidence.
No downstream consumer harm is yet proven.

architecture_delta.decision: Keep semantic AST identity and parser/grammar contract identity as explicitly separate layers. Do not rename or migrate persisted hashes until downstream consumers are traced and current-checkout parity executes.

targeted_distribution.claycode: Add current-checkout semantic-layer parity after the selected grammar lane stabilizes; reuse one production parser constructor.
targeted_distribution.unifieddb: Trace syntax/semantic/contract hashes used for cache identity, replay equality, deduplication or promotion.
targeted_distribution.harness: Treat parser-contract hash drift as provenance/version drift rather than cognitive semantic delta unless a differential proves otherwise.

next_falsifier: On current exact checkout, parse admitted G9+Dialect through production frontend and standalone canonicalizer with one shared parser constructor; assert semantic-layer parity separately from grammar-bound contract identity, then trace every persisted hash consumer.
